PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. # Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal – not for transmission to Seller

---

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

Before the substantive issues, one point governs how we read the whole package. The Seller's preamble asserts that the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," reflect the "agreed commercial bargain," and are "marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened."

**We should not accept that characterisation.** Under our playbook:

- A 20% / AUD 4.8m cap is a conditional fallback usable **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **None has been given.**
- An 18-month claims period is likewise a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval. **None has been given.**

The Seller's statement that these were agreed at principal level is unsupported by anything in our record. It is either a misunderstanding on their side or a negotiating tactic. Either way, our response should state plainly that the Buyer has not agreed these positions, no principal-level approval has been given, and the "FINAL" label is not accepted. The "market context" paragraph (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers as "standard") is advocacy, not evidence, and should carry no weight in our mark-up.

Also note the Disclosure Letter's own reservation at [11] ("No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included") directly contradicts the Seller Update's claim that positions were agreed. We can use that inconsistency.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General warranty cap (cl 12.1)

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (opening); 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority |

**Departure:** Seller has landed directly on our unauthorised fallback. **Push back:** revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not concede 20% without obtaining Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this specific draft. Do not let the Seller's "agreed at principal level" assertion substitute for that authority.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once basket exceeded | Excess only (deductible) | From first dollar (tipping basket) |

**Departure:** Three separate departures, each materially adverse. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the basket is structured as a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined, the Seller's structure means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is simply unrecoverable, and any individual claim under AUD 25,000 never counts at all. **Push back on all three:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar recovery.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)

**Departure:** 18 months vs our 24-month opening position. Same analysis as the cap – 18 months is an unauthorised fallback. **Push back:** 24 months.

**Separate and more serious:** the Seller proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This is a drafting device that would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant claims into the general regime by default. It directly conflicts with our requirement to keep categories separate with no hidden general-regime override. **Reject the default-application language** and require the reverse: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and nothing else unless expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties

**Departure:** Seller proposes capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

This is a major departure. A title failure means the Buyer may not own what it paid AUD 24m for; capping that at 20% and time-limiting it to 18 months is not acceptable. **Push back:** separate Fundamental/Title regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 4.8m ceiling on a title claim.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

**Departure:** The Seller's wording applies caps, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to every Claim "of any nature." Nothing in the Seller Update carves out fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.

This is a red-line item. Our playbook requires those matters carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one on our side may waive this. The Seller's draft, read literally, would purport to limit the Seller's liability for its own fraud. **Push back:** insist on an express, comprehensive fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that overrides every limitation provision. This is non-negotiable on our side regardless of what is conceded elsewhere.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])

**Departure:** Seller relies on general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 September 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records.

This is exactly the whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure our playbook rejects. If accepted, any fact buried anywhere in the data room or in any public register would qualify every warranty, regardless of whether the Buyer could reasonably have identified it. **Push back:** disclosure must be specific and fair – identifying the matter, the warranty it qualifies, and sufficient detail for the Buyer to understand its nature and scope. Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures; the data room should be disclosed only to the extent specific documents are cross-referenced against specific warranties.

Note also [1.4] (nothing in the letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent/payment/notice is required). This is a standard reservation but it cuts both ways: if the Seller won't admit anything, the letter cannot be relied on as fair disclosure of the matters it reserves on. We should point this out.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

**Departure:** Blanket exclusion for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

This compounds the disclosure problem. "Discoverable" is not the same as "known"; this would impute to the Buyer constructive knowledge of everything in the data room and every public record, and extend it to advisers. **Push back:** delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be (a) limited to actual knowledge, (b) of named individuals, (c) after reasonable enquiry of named Seller knowledge persons, and (d) never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

Context: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Clause 11.2 contains change-control consent and clause 11.3 contains conditions on that consent.

**Departure:** Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

Two problems. First, reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a consent covering 30% of revenue. Second, consent-on-delivery ignores clause 11.3 – a consent subject to unsatisfied conditions is not an effective consent. The Disclosure Letter [2] confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions is in the data room**. **Push back:** the condition precedent must require (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent and (b) documentary evidence that the 11.3 conditions have been met, both delivered before Completion. The Seller's endeavours obligation should be stronger than "reasonable."

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

Context: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-control at 8.1; discharge at 9.2. Disclosure Letter [3] confirms the facility has **not** been repaid and no final discharge of security is in the data room.

**Departure:** Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion."

This is unacceptable on a debt-free/cash-free deal. The Buyer would complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the Company and only a promise of a later release. **Push back:** require (a) a current payout letter from Riverlark, (b) direct repayment of the facility from Completion funds at Completion, and (c) effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which exists. Also check whether the 8.1 change-of-control trigger has been addressed independently of repayment.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses – DD-005 (Funds flow)

Context: AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses; conditions are Completion plus continued employment. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms these **do not appear** in the draft funds flow and that the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Departure:** Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not itemised them. That is internally inconsistent: if they are the Seller's cost, they need to be in the funds flow as a Seller-borne item; if they are not in the funds flow, the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) ends up paying them.

**Push back:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any leave-loading or similar) must be either a specific line item funded from the Seller's proceeds at Completion or expressly treated as Seller-funded with a corresponding adjustment. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. The funds flow must not be allowed to silently exclude them.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

Context: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. Disclosure Letter [4] confirms this is not independent bank verification and that no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Departure:** Seller says the existing narrow indemnity (limited to the SOW3 payment) is "adequate."

The indemnity covers only the payment, not the consequence of non-payment – i.e. that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials. **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover title/ownership defects in the Ironquay deliverables and any loss arising from non-transfer, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism (pay the outstanding amount and obtain confirmatory assignment). Note internally: the AUD 180,000 figure is **not independently verified in either direction** – we should not assert that it is unpaid, nor accept that it is; require a confirmatory assignment and payment receipt as a Completion deliverable.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident – DD-006 (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

Context: download link delivered to an unintended external email address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification requirement are **unknown** as at 22 September 2026; investigation remains preliminary; no loss amount stated.

**Departure:** Seller characterises it as "a preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."

That conclusion is premature on the Seller's own disclosure – they do not know whether the file was accessed. **Our position (consistent with playbook): assume no confirmed breach, no confirmed harm, no confirmed notification duty and no numeric demand in either direction.** But we should require: (a) log preservation and a proper investigation, (b) periodic updates through to Completion, (c) a specific warranty/indemnity in Schedule 6 covering any loss if the matter develops, and (d) an obligation to notify the Buyer before any regulator or data-subject notification. We should not accept the "not material" label, nor should we overstate the matter as a breach.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals – DD-008 / DD-011

Context: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 aggregate; Disclosure Letter [8] says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Departure (modest):** Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs."

Our playbook says **assess** – no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction. **Action:** ask the Seller to confirm, for each renewal, whether it is committed/unavoidable, the term and termination rights, and whether any amount has accrued pre-Completion. Depending on the answers, this may be a working-capital / completion-accounts point rather than a price deduction. Do not push a Debt classification without the facts.

### 2.14 Tax / IP

**Departure:** Seller treats Tax and IP as "settled under the general regime above."

This is not agreed. Our playbook keeps Tax and IP as separate categories and currently **OPEN**. **Push back:** reject their inclusion in the general regime; reserve the position. Internally, do not assume unlimited liability on these, and do not treat them as resolved.

### 2.15 Title evidence

**Departure:** Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register.

Disclosure Letter [10] itself concedes the register is "the source relied on for title" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is a Seller-supplied internal document; it is not independent proof. **Push back / action:** require independent evidence – ASIC extracts, board minutes and share certificates, confirmation of no encumbrances (including PPSR search), evidence of Seller's authority, and a title warranty with the Fundamental regime above. This also links to Riverlark: we need to confirm whether the Riverlark security extends to the shares.

### 2.16 Minor points (lease, Mossvale)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only; not described as landlord consent. Confirm the notification is given pre-Completion and that no consent is in fact required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment; no indication consent is needed on a share sale. Confirm by reference to the actual clause that there is no change-of-control trigger. Low priority but should be closed off.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable / red-line**
1. Reject the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing in writing; no Amelia Frost authority exists for 20% cap or 18 months.
2. Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
3. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
4. Delete the "any limitation applies to all Claims" default; keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate.
5. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion – not post-Completion.
6. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence of 11.3 conditions satisfied, delivered pre-Completion.

**Revert to playbook opening positions**
7. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
8. Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
9. Claims period: 24 months.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
10. Delete whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
11. Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3); any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named persons after enquiry of named Seller persons, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Specific matters**
12. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a Seller-funded line item in the funds flow; obtain written confirmation on superannuation/payroll tax.
13. Ironquay: broaden indemnity to cover ownership of SOW3 materials; preserve cure; require payment receipt and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; do not assume the AUD 180,000 is or isn't paid.
14. DD-006 incident: reject "not material" label; require log preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity; assume no confirmed breach or quantum in either direction.
15. Sandbar: request facts on each renewal before taking a position; no automatic Debt classification.
16. Tax/IP: reject inclusion in general regime; keep open.
17. Title: require independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authority); DD-012 is not sufficient.
18. Close off lease notification and Mossvale change-of-control queries.

**Internal action items**
- Confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been or will be given before our response issues.
- Do not transmit any part of this memo or the playbook to the Seller.

**Departure:** Blanket exclusion for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

This compounds the disclosure problem. "Discoverable" is not the same as "known"; this would impute to the Buyer constructive knowledge of everything in the data room and every public record, and extend it to advisers. **Push back:** delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be (a) limited to actual knowledge, (b) of named individuals, (c) after reasonable enquiry of named Seller knowledge persons, and (d) never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

Context: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Clause 11.2 contains change-control consent and clause 11.3 contains conditions on that consent.

**Departure:** Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

Two problems. First, reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a consent covering 30% of revenue. Second, consent-on-delivery ignores clause 11.3 – a consent subject to unsatisfied conditions is not an effective consent. The Disclosure Letter [2] confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions is in the data room**. **Push back:** the condition precedent must require (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent and (b) documentary evidence that the 11.3 conditions have been met, both delivered before Completion. The Seller's endeavours obligation should be stronger than "reasonable."

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

Context: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-control at 8.1; discharge at 9.2. Disclosure Letter [3] confirms the facility has **not** been repaid and no final discharge of security is in the data room.

**Departure:** Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion."

This is unacceptable on a debt-free/cash-free deal. The Buyer would complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the Company and only a promise of a later release. **Push back:** require (a) a current payout letter from Riverlark, (b) direct repayment of the facility from Completion funds at Completion, and (c) effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which exists. Also check whether the 8.1 change-of-control trigger has been addressed independently of repayment.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses – DD-005 (Funds flow)

Context: AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses; conditions are Completion plus continued employment. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms these **do not appear** in the draft funds flow and that the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Departure:** Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not itemised them. That is internally inconsistent: if they are the Seller's cost, they need to be in the funds flow as a Seller-borne item; if they are not in the funds flow, the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) ends up paying them.

**Push back:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any leave-loading or similar) must be either a specific line item funded from the Seller's proceeds at Completion or expressly treated as Seller-funded with a corresponding adjustment. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. The funds flow must not be allowed to silently exclude them.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

Context: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. Disclosure Letter [4] confirms this is not independent bank verification and that no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Departure:** Seller says the existing narrow indemnity (limited to the SOW3 payment) is "adequate."

The indemnity covers only the payment, not the consequence of non-payment – i.e. that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials. **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover title/ownership defects in the Ironquay deliverables and any loss arising from non-transfer, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism (pay the outstanding amount and obtain confirmatory assignment). Note internally: the AUD 180,000 figure is **not independently verified in either direction** – we should not assert that it is unpaid, nor accept that it is; require a confirmatory assignment and payment receipt as a Completion deliverable.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident – DD-006 (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

Context: download link delivered to an unintended external email address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification requirement are **unknown** as at 22 September 2026; investigation remains preliminary; no loss amount stated.

**Departure:** Seller characterises it as "a preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."

That conclusion is premature on the Seller's own disclosure – they do not know whether the file was accessed. **Our position (consistent with playbook): assume no confirmed breach, no confirmed harm, no confirmed notification duty and no numeric demand in either direction.** But we should require: (a) log preservation and a proper investigation, (b) periodic updates through to Completion, (c) a specific warranty/indemnity in Schedule 6 covering any loss if the matter develops, and (d) an obligation to notify the Buyer before any regulator or data-subject notification. We should not accept the "not material" label, nor should we overstate the matter as a breach.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals – DD-008 / DD-011

Context: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 aggregate; Disclosure Letter [8] says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Departure (modest):** Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs."

Our playbook says **assess** – no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction. **Action:** ask the Seller to confirm, for each renewal, whether it is committed/unavoidable, the term and termination rights, and whether any amount has accrued pre-Completion. Depending on the answers, this may be a working-capital / completion-accounts point rather than a price deduction. Do not push a Debt classification without the facts.

### 2.14 Tax / IP

**Departure:** Seller treats Tax and IP as "settled under the general regime above."

This is not agreed. Our playbook keeps Tax and IP as separate categories and currently **OPEN**. **Push back:** reject their inclusion in the general regime; reserve the position. Internally, do not assume unlimited liability on these, and do not treat them as resolved.

### 2.15 Title evidence

**Departure:** Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register.

Disclosure Letter [10] itself concedes the register is "the source relied on for title" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is a Seller-supplied internal document; it is not independent proof. **Push back / action:** require independent evidence – ASIC extracts, board minutes and share certificates, confirmation of no encumbrances (including PPSR search), evidence of Seller's authority, and a title warranty with the Fundamental regime above. This also links to Riverlark: we need to confirm whether the Riverlark security extends to the shares.

### 2.16 Minor points (lease, Mossvale)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only; not described as landlord consent. Confirm the notification is given pre-Completion and that no consent is in fact required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment; no indication consent is needed on a share sale. Confirm by reference to the actual clause that there is no change-of-control trigger. Low priority but should be closed off.

**Non-negotiable / red-line**
1. Reject the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing in writing; no Amelia Frost authority exists for 20% cap or 18 months.
2. Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
3. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
4. Delete the "any limitation applies to all Claims" default; keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate.
5. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion – not post-Completion.
6. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence of 11.3 conditions satisfied, delivered pre-Completion.

**Revert to playbook opening positions**
7. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
8. Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
9. Claims period: 24 months.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
10. Delete whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
11. Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3); any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named persons after enquiry of named Seller persons, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Specific matters**

14. DD-006 incident: reject "not material" label; require log preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity; assume no confirmed breach or quantum in either direction.
15. Sandbar: request facts on each renewal before taking a position; no automatic Debt classification.
16. Tax/IP: reject inclusion in general regime; keep open.
17. Title: require independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authority); DD-012 is not sufficient.
18. Close off lease notification and Mossvale change-of-control queries.
